_comment: Every dataset the build uses, pinned to an exact git commit. `atlas fetch` checks out only the listed files and records their SHA-256 in data/raw/manifest.lock.json; `atlas build` refuses to run if a file no longer matches its recorded hash. Change a commit here to upgrade a source; the build output records which commits it came from.

sources.title: OpenBible.info Cross References
sources.provides: About 340,000 verse-to-verse cross-references with community vote weights (derived from the Treasury of Scripture Knowledge and user votes).
sources.attribution: Cross references from OpenBible.info, CC BY 4.0
sources.note: openbible.info publishes the file directly; this build reads the unmodified copy mirrored in scrollmapper/bible_databases so the input is pinned by git commit.

sources.title: Berean Standard Bible (BSB), USFM edition with footnotes and section headings
sources.provides: The BSB's own footnotes. In the New Testament they name the Old Testament verse behind each quotation, sometimes adding "see also LXX" for the Septuagint; in the Old Testament they list where a verse is cited in the New. The Quotations notes are read from them. Its section headings, and the parallel passages they name such as "Jesus Heals a Paralytic (Matthew 9:1–8; Luke 5:17–26)", are where the Parallels notes start.
sources.attribution: The Holy Bible, Berean Standard Bible, BSB is produced in cooperation with Bible Hub, Discovery Bible, OpenBible.com, and the Berean Bible Translation Committee. This text of God's Word has been dedicated to the public domain.
sources.note: A USFM copy of the BSB published by the usfm-bible project as an example of USFM markup: per its README, a fork of the text as of 26 August 2024 with the licensing unchanged. Only its footnotes and section headings are used; the English the app shows comes from the BSB entry listed separately.

sources.title: Berean Standard Bible (BSB)
sources.provides: English text of all 66 books. Used for search, the word-to-word links, and as the default reading text.
sources.attribution: The Holy Bible, Berean Standard Bible, BSB is produced in cooperation with Bible Hub, Discovery Bible, OpenBible.com, and the Berean Bible Translation Committee. This text of God's Word has been dedicated to the public domain.

sources.title: Nave's Topical Bible (Orville J. Nave, 1896), as a table
sources.provides: About 5,300 subjects, each with the verses Nave listed for it. Ask the Bible uses it as an index only, to gather the verses on a question or subject; none of Nave's own wording is shown.
sources.license: CC BY 4.0 (this edition); Nave's Topical Bible itself is public domain
sources.attribution: Nave's Topical Dictionary from BibleData by Brady Stephenson, github.com/BradyStephenson/bible-data (CC BY 4.0)

sources.title: King James Version (1769)
sources.provides: English text used only by search, so a verse typed in King James wording is found. Never shown.
sources.attribution: King James Version (1769), public domain

sources.title: American Standard Version (1901)
sources.provides: English text used only by search, so a verse typed in the wording of the ASV or the modern translations built on it is found. Never shown.
sources.attribution: American Standard Version (1901), public domain

sources.title: OpenBible.info Bible Geocoding Data
sources.provides: The places the Bible names, the verses that name them, the modern sites proposed for each place and how confident each identification is. Used for the Places line and map.
sources.attribution: Bible Geocoding Data from OpenBible.info, CC BY 4.0
sources.note: Coordinates the dataset credits to OpenStreetMap (ODbL), Google Maps or the Google Earth community, or takes from a Palestine Grid reference (epsg_28191), are left out; where it gives its own position for a site (custom_lonlat), that one is used. A place is listed under a verse only where the BSB text names it.

sources.title: OpenBible.info Bible Geocoding Data: region shapes
sources.provides: The shapes OpenBible.info drew for regions, valleys and wildernesses (Galilee, Edom, the Valley of Elah). Used to shade a region on the Places map. Where it gives bands of confidence, the middle band is used.
sources.attribution: Bible Geocoding Data from OpenBible.info, CC BY 4.0
sources.note: Only shapes the dataset drew itself (format 'kml' in data/geometry.jsonl) are listed: those taken from OpenStreetMap (ODbL), islands, which Natural Earth already draws, and generated circles are left out. The list is the best identification's shape for each place, as extra_real_map.rs picks it; a place whose shape is not listed is drawn without one.

sources.title: Theographic Bible Metadata
sources.provides: People tied to each place: who was born there, who died there and who was there; and the events that happened at each place, with Theographic's dates. Events are shown in the Places map at Study, people and dates at Deep.
sources.attribution: Theographic Bible Metadata by Robert Rouse (viz.bible), CC BY-SA 4.0
sources.note: The files built from it, extras/real-map/people.json and extras/real-map/events.json, are shared under the same license, CC BY-SA 4.0. Event years are Theographic's own, from one traditional chronology (Creation in 4004 BC, the Exodus in 1491 BC), and are shown only at Deep with that said.

sources.title: Natural Earth
sources.provides: Coastlines, lakes, rivers, sea names and modern borders, cut to the Bible lands and simplified for the Places map.
sources.attribution: Made with Natural Earth. Free vector and raster map data @ naturalearthdata.com.
sources.note: The coastlines and rivers are today's; the borders are used only to name the modern country of places far from Jerusalem.

sources.title: Digital Syriac Corpus: the Peshitta New Testament (Syriac)
sources.provides: The New Testament in Syriac, a dialect of Aramaic: the Peshitta, translated from the Greek around AD 350-450, as printed by the British and Foreign Bible Society (1905), with vowel points. 2 Peter, 2 and 3 John, Jude, Revelation and John 7:53-8:11, which the early Peshitta did not have, come from later Syriac translations. Shown at Deep beside the English, as a translation and never as Jesus' own words.
sources.license: CC BY 4.0 (TEI XML edition); the Syriac base text is public domain
sources.attribution: Syriac text from the Digital Syriac Corpus (syriaccorpus.org): TEI XML edition by James E. Walters, CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Base text: The New Testament in Syriac (British and Foreign Bible Society, 1905), public domain; Syriac text transcribed by George A. Kiraz.
sources.note: The repository has no file 125; the build checks that each file's header names its book and carries the CC BY 4.0 license. The source marks the text as an uncorrected transcription, not yet fully proofread against the printed edition. Changes made: whitespace is collapsed; the transcription's '+' marks before some plural words (51, in Matthew) are removed; four places are moved onto the BSB's verse numbers: Luke 10:42 (coded inside chapter 11), Matthew 23:13-14 (the two woes in the other order), Romans 16:24-27 (the closing blessing numbered 16:27, where the BSB's footnoted 16:24 has it) and 3 John 1:15 (joined to 1:14, as in the BSB). An approximate romanization is added by this app, read from the vowel points.

sources.title: Tyndale Open Bible Dictionary
sources.provides: When each part of the Bible happened and when each book was written: eras, dated events and dating views, quoted word for word from the dictionary's articles and its two charts of significant events and dates.
sources.attribution: Adapted from Tyndale Open Bible Dictionary. The original work by Tyndale House Publishers is available for free at http://www.tyndaleopenresources.com. Copyright (C) 2023 by Tyndale House Publishers. Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/
sources.note: Only tyndale-source-files/ (Tyndale's unmodified package) is read; adapted-articles/ is not used. Every quotation shown in the app is checked word for word against these files at build time.

sources.title: Easton's Bible Dictionary (1897), the Christian Classics Ethereal Library's edition, as kept in NEUU's Bible Dictionary Dataset
sources.provides: Every entry of Easton's Bible Dictionary, with the verses each one cites. Readable in the app from the Sources shelf, and offered under the verses an entry cites.
sources.license: Public domain (the dictionary, in CCEL's transcription, which CCEL marks public domain); carried by CCEL Paragraphs (CC BY-SA 4.0) and the Bible Dictionary Dataset (CC BY 4.0)
sources.attribution: Easton's Bible Dictionary by M. G. Easton (1897), public domain, in the Christian Classics Ethereal Library's transcription (marked public domain). Via CCEL Paragraphs by Jon Craton, huggingface.co/datasets/jncraton/ccel-paragraphs, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/), and the Bible Dictionary Dataset, Copyright (c) 2026 NEUU, github.com/neuu-org/bible-dictionary-dataset, licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); modified as described in NOTICE.md.
sources.note: The build reads the CCEL ThML file the dataset keeps, not the dataset's JSON, which cuts long entries at 5,000 characters. Only the dictionary's own words and the verse references CCEL marked up are used, never anything CCEL wrote (such as its description of the book). Changes made: a term the edition gives twice (Kadesh, Salmon) is one entry, verse references become links, and a second entry with the same address (Hail!) gets its own. The files built from it (dict/easton/, extras/dictionary/) are shared under CC BY-SA 4.0.

sources.title: Smith's Bible Dictionary, the Christian Classics Ethereal Library's edition, as kept in NEUU's Bible Dictionary Dataset
sources.provides: Every entry of Smith's Bible Dictionary, with the verses each one cites. Readable in the app from the Sources shelf, and offered under the verses an entry cites.
sources.license: Public domain (the dictionary, in CCEL's transcription, which CCEL marks public domain); carried by CCEL Paragraphs (CC BY-SA 4.0) and the Bible Dictionary Dataset (CC BY 4.0)
sources.attribution: Smith's Bible Dictionary by William Smith, public domain, in the Christian Classics Ethereal Library's transcription (marked public domain). Via CCEL Paragraphs by Jon Craton, huggingface.co/datasets/jncraton/ccel-paragraphs, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/), and the Bible Dictionary Dataset, Copyright (c) 2026 NEUU, github.com/neuu-org/bible-dictionary-dataset, licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); modified as described in NOTICE.md.
sources.note: The build reads the CCEL ThML file the dataset keeps, not the dataset's JSON, which leaves out the numbered lists that make up much of Smith's (687 entries lose text there, and 73 lose all of it) and cuts long entries at 5,000 characters. CCEL dates its print source 1884, the year of the American edition revised and edited by F. N. and M. A. Peloubet; notes marked ED. are the editors'. Smith's dictionary first appeared in 1860-1863. Only the dictionary's own words and the verse references CCEL marked up are used, never anything CCEL wrote. Changes made: list items become numbered paragraphs, verse references become links, names given in title case keep their small words lowercase (Ark of the Covenant), and the edition's 'High Places6813 Priest' is named High Priest. The files built from it (dict/smith/, extras/dictionary/) are shared under CC BY-SA 4.0.

sources.title: Aquifer Open Study Notes (English), adapted from Tyndale Open Study Notes
sources.provides: Study notes on almost every passage of the Bible, written by Bible scholars at Tyndale House Publishers and adapted into plain English by Mission Mutual. Shown one tap away from a verse, as notes from these scholars and never as the app's own claim.
sources.attribution: Aquifer Open Study Notes, (C) 2026 Mission Mutual, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/). It is an adaptation of Tyndale Open Study Notes, (C) 2023 Tyndale House Publishers (https://tyndaleopenresources.com), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0.
sources.note: Only the English JSON files are read. Changes made: each note's HTML is reduced to paragraphs, lists, italics and verse references (links and empty headings are dropped); verse references are placed on the BSB's numbering, and any the BSB does not have are left as plain text. The adapted data (web/public/data/extras/notes/) is shared under the same license, CC BY-SA 4.0.

sources.provides: Hand-made links from each Hebrew, Aramaic and Greek word to the BSB English words that translate it (Hebrew from the WLC as tokenized by Macula, Greek from the Berean Greek New Testament). Used to color matching words in word-by-word mode.
sources.license: CC BY 4.0 (alignments); the WLC and the BSB are public domain
sources.attribution: Word alignments from Clear Bible / Biblica, github.com/Clear-Bible/Alignments (CC BY 4.0)

sources.title: MACULA Hebrew Linguistic Datasets
sources.provides: For each Hebrew word of the Old Testament, the Greek word the Septuagint (the Greek Old Testament) uses at that place, with its Strong's number. Used to pair the Greek words of a New Testament quotation with the Hebrew words they stand for.
sources.license: CC BY 4.0 (the Westminster Leningrad Codex it annotates is public domain)
sources.attribution: MACULA Hebrew Linguistic Datasets, available at https://github.com/Clear-Bible/macula-hebrew/ (© Biblica, Inc., CC BY 4.0)
sources.note: Only the word ids, Hebrew text and the 'greek' and 'greekstrong' columns are read. The file is stored with Git LFS, so `atlas fetch` downloads it from GitHub's media server and checks it against the pointer's SHA-256. MACULA's LICENSE.md lists 'Greek equivalents drawn from the Septuagint' among the data it licenses CC BY 4.0. Nothing from the file is published: the build writes only word positions.

sources.title: Strong's Hebrew and Greek dictionaries (Open Scriptures JSON)
sources.provides: Which Hebrew and Greek words come from which. Used for each word's family of related words in the word study.
sources.license: CC BY-SA (JSON edition); Strong's dictionaries (1890) are public domain
sources.attribution: James Strong, Exhaustive Concordance of the Bible (1890, public domain); JSON edition by Open Scriptures, github.com/openscriptures/strongs (CC BY-SA), Greek from the XML by Ulrik Petersen
sources.note: Only each entry's derivation line is used, to link a word to the word it comes from. Strong's definitions are not shown. Guesses ('perhaps', 'probably', 'apparently', 'akin to'), links that rest on a sense the reader can't see, comparisons and compounds of two words are left out, except a Greek word built on a prefix (as ἐξέρχομαι on ἔρχομαι). 'From the same as' and 'from the base of' a word that is not a verb make two words share a root. Where one number covers words that only look alike, the link goes to the one with nearly all the uses or a sense checked by hand. A short hand-checked list corrects slips in Strong's numbers (see NOTICE.md).
